https://telecom.economictimes.indiatimes.text: BUDAPEST: Hungarian Prime Minister Peter Magyar said on Monday his government will review contracts signed between the state and Hungarian IT and telecoms company 4iG ‌while the ⁠former ⁠government of Viktor Orban was in power.The news sent 4iG's ​shares sharply lower, down more than 11% in late afternoon ​trade and on course for their biggest one-day loss since Magyar's election in April.4iG did not ​immediately respond to a request ⁠for comment."The ‌government has ordered a review ​of all ​their contracts with the state," Magyar said ⁠in a post on Facebook, adding that the ​company had acquired assets of strategic ​importance under Orban's government.4iG has interests in the telecoms sector, IT, defense and the space industry.Magyar said, among other inquiries, there was a review underway of a framework deal worth more ‌than 1.3 trillion forints ($4.2 billion) signed weeks before the April elections between 4iG and the ​defense ministry.He ​said the ⁠government would make the findings of its reviews public and, in case of any irregularities, it would turn the ​information over to the relevant authorities.Oligarchs close to Orban and his government expanded their influence in strategic sectors after he gained power in 2010.

https://www.dw.com/en/propaganda-in-russ.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5NE46 Patriotism has become a core part of the national curriculum since 2022 Image: Konstanin Kokoshkin/Pivcario/picture alliance Advertisement Earlier this year, several schools in Novosibirsk, a city of 1.6 million in southern Siberia, received a textbook on patriotism from the authorities. According to students, with whom DW spoke to on condition of anonymity, in the book the authors urge children to prepare themselves to die for their country. Furthermore, they equate homosexuality with pedophilia and Disney cartoons with pornography, and give instructions on how women should use their "charms." Europeans are described as "thieves, murderers and liars." The textbook, which provides "materials for spiritual, moral, and patriotic upbringing" is supposed to be used as part of "patriotism lessons" that have been on the curriculum since 2022 . Though it is not included on the national list of core curriculum books, the content reflects the Kremlin's intentions to spread propaganda in educational institutions. 'Love always involves sacrifice.' One of the main topics of the book is the war in Ukraine and the idea that dying for one's country is a blessing is repeated several times: "Love always involves sacrifice," writes one of the authors. "The sacrifice of a defender of the homeland is their life." Elsewhere in the book, the authors make constant claims that Russia is better than Western countries. They also say that children are "mentally crippled" because of "computer games, Hollywood action films, pornography and Disney cartoons." They argue that European nations that used to be colonial empires legitimized "murder, lies and plunder" through the conquest and subjugation of new territories. Russia, on the other hand, "never exploited its numerous peoples," they say, but merely improved their living conditions. The book makes no mention of the culture of Indigenous peoples in what is Russia today, or of any religions other than Christianity and "Slavic paganism." This textbook is used in certain Russian schools to teach children about patriotism and other subjects Image: M. Remaevich 'More cannon fodder' For Ilya, a 16-year-old student in Novosibirsk who has read the book and whose name has been changed, the idea of dying for his country is anathema. "It's proof that the country wants more cannon fodder," he told DW, adding that "dying for the country" actually meant dying for "the president's interests and ambitions." He said that a few years ago, he had started watching the videos of Alexei Navalny, the Kremlin critic and opposition leader who died in jail in 2024 "more for fun than for any other reason." He said it was Navalny's 2021 investigation into Russian President Vladimir Putin's Black Sea palace that had first drawn his attention. But it was when the authorities decided to block access to the US platforms YouTube and Discord that he began to oppose the government. He set up a VPN out of "contrariness" he said, looking for information about other opposition figures and reading the independent media. As he found out more about the cruelty and senselessness of the war, he criticized the government more strongly. He confirmed that propaganda had become an integral part of the curriculum in the past four years. On top of the "Conversations about Important Things" that take place every Monday morning, there are now also subjects such as "Fundamentals of Homeland Security and Defense." He said that people who have taken part in the war in Ukraine are invited to lessons focusing on students' future and decisions regarding what career path to take. Even outside of the classroom, students are encouraged to be "patriotic." Ilya said that a student had been reprimanded by the principal for wearing a sweater with a slogan written in English on it. "Young man, do you realize that your sweater has words on it in the language of unfriendly countries?" she reportedly asked him. "A call to the Federal Security Service will take care of that!" Ilya also recalled that a school assembly held to mark May 9, which commemorates the Soviet Union's victory over Nazi Germany in 1945, the principal and her deputy had compared what is known in Russia as the " Great Patriotic War " to the current war in Ukraine. They had said that Russia would once again be steadfast and emerge victorious. Students are taught about being a soldier and told it is an honor to die for the country Image: Konstantin Kokoshkin/Picvario/Russian Look/Global Look Press/picture alliance 'I love freedom' Alexei (name changed), another 16-year-old student in Novosibirsk, told DW that many of his classmates avoided going to "patriotic events." He too said that the blocking of YouTube had made a difference to him. "I looked into why it was blocked," he said. "Because nothing happens by chance. And that's how my interest in politics began." That's when he realized that the authorities wanted to get rid of inconvenient citizens and suppress free speech. "I love freedom, so it was hard," he said. Ilya thinks that most students don't take the propaganda seriously. "On the one hand, we laugh about it in class, at least my friends do," he said. "On the other, we don't care. Some simply don't listen. We're very good at being quiet and not talking much about it," Dima Zicer is an educator and the author of the Russian-language podcast "Love, Don't Discipline" who moved to Estonia after the full-scale invasion of Ukraine . He told DW that "many students are happy to be part of a pro-Putin majority that doesn't think about things, according to the principle: 'We'll crush them all; we're stronger than everyone else. Everyone will be scared of us.'" He said that there was no statistical data to back his argument, but he said that he had drawn his conclusions from his extensive experience working with Russian children, as well as his communication with parents. He said that these often only became aware of how serious the situation was when their children started saying things such as "We'll crush them" or "Putin is great," as well as talking about supposed Nazis and fascists in Ukraine. Alexei and Ilya, who think differently and want the war in Ukraine to end, are worried about the unstable situation in Russia. They want to leave the country after graduating. https://www.zf.ro/bt-investor-day/who-br.text: Leu / EUR 5.3370 Leu / GBP 6.3104 Leu / USD 4.7571 Who brings liquidity to the Bucharest Stock Exchange BT Capital Partners intermed-iated 34.7% of the value of bond transactions on the Bucharest Stock Exchange (BVB) in the first eight months of 2026, ahead of BCR, with 20.2%, and Tradeville, with 17.7%, according to the BVB ranking. Of the 19.4 billion lei (3.7 billion euros) intermediated by the company in 2026 at the BVB, 9.5 billion lei (1.8 billion euros) came from bonds and 10 billion lei (1.9 billion euros) from shares and fund units. In August 2026 alone, BT Capital Partners accounted for 38.6% of bond transactions. BT Capital Partners was the lead manager of the syndicate that intermediated this year's ninth Fidelis government bond offer carried out in September. Through this round, the Ministry of Finance raised 847 million lei (162 million euros) and investors placed 11,492 subscription orders. Since August 2020, through 40 Fidelis offers, the Romanian state has raised 72.4 billion lei (14.5 billion euros) from the general population, of which over 10.4 billion lei (almost 2 billion euros) in 2026, according to the BVB. In 2025, BT Capital Partners was co-manager for the bond issuances worth 500 million euros each launched by Romgaz, Electrica, and Banca Transilvania. According to company data, over the last ten years, it has participated in issuances on external markets through which Romanian issuers raised over 7 billion euros. Daniela Secară, CEO of BT Capital Partners, told the ZF Capital Market conference that it is hard to find investors for the bonds of an unlisted company. Pension funds, for instance, can only invest in companies that are publicly listed, hold an investment-grade rating, or are state-owned. Therefore, discussions with issuers are currently focused more on stock listings. In April 2026, the BT Group launched its first Exchange-Traded Fund (ETF). It is an instrument that provides retail investors with simplified exposure to the leading companies listed on the Bucharest Stock Exchange. „We have seen many investors transition from Fidelis to the ETFs, and their next step is to venture into the capital market and equity investments independently,‟ said Daniela Secară, adding that retail investors are now focusing more on medium- and long-term investments rather than on speculative trading. BT Capital Partners describes its role as building an efficient mechanism through which public savings and institutional capital are directed toward companies that generate investments, jobs, and economic growth. Some retail investors are now locking in the profits they made over the last two years, the CEO of BT Capital Partners added. The market's evolution also depends on the country's credit rating. „Yes, foreign investors, in particular, focus on this rating aspect, but Romanian pension and investment funds drive the vast majority of the capital market.‟ According to the CEO, institutional investors are in no rush to exit companies and businesses. We believe the next chapter of the capital market will be defined by stronger companies, a larger number of investors, and the continuous integration of Romania into the global economic structure. BT Capital Partners aims to remain a promoter and an active partner in this transformation," Daniela Secară pointed out. https://www.dw.com/en/france-confirms-fi.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5OXvr The Shamonda virus has been detected in animals in Africa and Japan for years and has been spreading across Europe Image: Boyer P/Andia.fr/imageBROKER/picture alliance Advertisement French health officials on Thursday confirmed that they had detected the Shamonda virus in a human — who died early this month — in what they say was the first-ever case of a human contracting the livestock disease. "Despite circulating in Africa and Asia for several decades, the Shamonda virus has never previously been detected in humans," said France 's Ministries of Health and of Agriculture in a joint statement. "No health risk to the general public identified at this time," they said, adding that the human infection appeared to be, "an exceptional case involving a severely immunocompromised patient." The World Health Organization (WHO) said the virus was unlikely to spread. "Based on current information and knowledge of ‌the transmission of closely related ‌viruses, ​this is an isolated human case and it is unlikely to ​lead to wider spread at this time," WHO told ⁠Reuters ​in a ​statement. French health officials say the livestock virus poses no theat to the public, pointing out that the first detected human infection was an exceedingly rare case Image: Alexis Jumeau/ABACAPRESS/IMAGO How is Shamonda virus transmitted? First ​identified in Nigeria in the mid-1960s, the insect-borne Shamonda virus is a variant of the Orthobunyavirus, a genus that contains 138 species, and primarily affects livestock, ‌particularly cattle. It is transmitted by culicoides, or biting midges. The virus has been detected in ​animals in Africa and Japan for years and has been spreading across Europe this year. Until now, it was not thought to be transmissible to humans. According to a press statement on the Ministry of Agriculture's webpage , "At this stage of the investigation, the hypothesis is that the case resulted from vector-borne transmission via the bite of a culicoid midge in eastern France, a region where the virus was reported to be circulating among animals in the spring and summer of 2026." The ministry said biological, clinical and epidemiological investigations are being carried out by experts in human, animal and environmental health, adding that authorities at the WHO and European Center for Disease Control had been notified of the incident.
